newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GRAND SLAM CUP -- THE MONEY ON OFFER.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAND SLAM CUP -- THE MONEY ON OFFER.

text.p: The Grand Slam Cup is the richest tournament in tennis with $6 million prize money.
The withdrawal through injury of world number one Pete Sampras, who would have earned a bonus of $250,000 for just turning up, has changed the prize money for players at the event, organisers said.
Sampras's bonus will be spread among the winnings of the other players.
Sweden's Thomas Enqvist also pulled out of the event with a shoulder injury on Tuesday and has been replaced by Spaniard Alex Corretja.
Here are the revised facts and figures about the event which began on Tuesday:
Established 1990 in Munich. Played on indoor carpet court in Munich's Olympic arena which was built for the 1972 Summer Games.
Participants - The best performers from the four grand slams of the year (Wimbledon and the French, U.S. and Australian Opens) qualify to take part in the 16-man knockout tournament.
Previous winners: 1990-Pete Sampras (U.S.), 1991-David Wheaton (U.S.), 1992-Michael Stich (Germany), 1993-Petr Korda (Czech Republic), 1994-Magnus Larsson (Sweden), 1995-Goran Ivanisevic (Croatia).
Prize money ($):
Winner: 1.625 million
Finalist: 812,500
Semifinalists: 431,250
Quarter-finalists: 262,500
First-round losers: 100,000
Reserves: 50,000
In addition, the winners of Wimbledon and three Opens are awarded $250,000 for playing in the Cup. If a player has won more than one grand slam he is awarded $250,000 for each victory.
Grand Slam champions participating in 1996: Becker (Australian Open), Yevgeny Kafelnikov (French Open), Richard Krajicek (Wimbledon)
First-round programme:
Tuesday - Stich v Tim Henman (Britain), Boris Becker (Germany) v Jason Stoltenberg (Australia), MaliVai Washington (U.S) v Krajicek (Netherlands), Marc Rosset (Switzerland) v Jim Courier (U.S.)

Wednesday (starting at 1200 GMT): Ivanisevic v Mikael Tillstrom (Sweden), Andre Agassi (U.S.) v Mark Woodforde (Australia), Jakob Hlasek (Switzerland) v Cedric Pioline (France), Kafelnikov (Russia) v Corretja
